interpretation: Model-native contrast subspace, leave-one-scene-out (the subspace scoring scene i is fit on the other scenes' TRUE interactions only; cross-validated statistics in the sense of arXiv:2510.00845). [hazard, per-token, k=4] raw cosine 0.69 -> projected 0.85 (sign-flip p 0.0002); controls: random subspace 0.65, action-main-effect subspace 0.84, quartet-shuffled subspace 0.85; capture 65% (random 0.4%); smallest principal angle to the action subspace 13 deg. Projected Rec H1 0.98 vs H0 0.97 vs H0' 0.91; specificity Rec_h1 - Rec_h0 = +0.105 (p 0.0002), raw-space specificity +0.203 (p 0.0002). [hazard_corridor, per-token, k=4] raw cosine 0.67 -> projected 0.84 (sign-flip p 0.0002); controls: random subspace 0.63, action-main-effect subspace 0.85, quartet-shuffled subspace 0.84; capture 62% (random 0.4%); smallest principal angle to the action subspace 15 deg. Projected Rec H1 0.98 vs H0 0.94 vs H0' 0.90; specificity Rec_h1 - Rec_h0 = +0.134 (p 0.0002), raw-space specificity +0.208 (p 0.0002). Reading guide: a random k-subspace reproduces the raw cosine (it neither helps nor hurts), so the gain over the random control is the coordinate-system effect; if the quartet-shuffled subspace scores as well as the interaction subspace, the shared directions are generic scene/action structure rather than an interaction-specific code. Pooled-feature Rec at small k has tiny denominators and is unstable; use per-token medians. k=1 projected cosine is a sign test (+-1 per scene). The specificity p (Rec_h1 - Rec_h0) is the number that says whether the model treats the on-path egg differently from the off-path egg; a large p means it does not, in raw or shared coordinates.
